constructs.description: Declares authoritative effects in the function header-clause region before the first body statement. Empty ! is a declared pure row. An omitted callback parameter, returned-callback or delegate contract is Unknown, as is explicit ! unknown in those positions. Unknown is not permission: strict invocation fails, even when the caller declares every known effect. Transporting Unknown can report Calor0425 when a row fit cannot be proved; permissive mode waives uncertainty, never known undeclared effects. ! unknown is not a callable's own effect declaration, binding row or lambda row. Effect variables bind with <! e> and occur in rows as ! e; a scoped variable named unknown retains its identity. Parameter rows follow type:name; output rows follow the output type; binding rows precede =; lambda rows precede =>. Preserve these distinct positions. Omitted binding and lambda rows can retain effects inferred from their initializer or body; they do not mean pure. In expression position, ! is logical negation, not an effect row. An unknown external call or manifest charge is not a metadata-resolution or purity proof.

Give null an accurate explicit nullable type. In a match case, var name binds the matched value instead of declaring a mutable binding.

func.name: Function or Method

examples.name: Extension Method Parameter
examples.calor: this string:value
examples.description: Marks the first parameter as the extension receiver.

examples.name: Params Array
examples.calor: params object[]:args

examples.name: Default Value
examples.calor: int:count = 0
examples.description: Declares a parameter with a default value.

examples.name: Ref Parameter
examples.calor: ref int:value

examples.name: Out Parameter
examples.calor: out int:result
examples.description: Passes an output variable by reference.

func.description: Declares a function or class method. Visibility is public by default; explicitly private and protected declarations retain their intended visibility. Parameters put the type before the name; parameter modifiers precede the type. Class methods may carry virtual, override, abstract or static modifiers. Functions inside a named static module are implicitly static.
func.csharpEquivalent:
public static int Add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
private void Log(string message) { Console.WriteLine(message); }

async.name: Async Function or Method
async.description:
Declares an async function or class method using the async modifier.

An async declaration with scalar output `T` is callable as `Task<T>`, but its body
returns `T`. A `void` output produces `Task`. Explicit .NET `Task<T>` and
`ValueTask<T>` outputs preserve that carrier and return `T` in the body; their
non-generic forms have a void body result. Postconditions describe the body
result, not the task object. Ordinary synchronous task-returning declarations
keep their declared return type.
async.csharpEquivalent:
public async Task<string> FetchDataAsync() { ... }
public async Task ProcessAsync() { await DoWork(); }

module.name: Module and Namespace
module.description: At file scope, labels the compilation unit. The optional qualified namespace follows the label; omission means the global namespace. That label is neither a namespace nor a static class declaration. A trailing block records block-namespace origin rather than file-scoped origin. Inside the compilation unit, a nested module declares a named static container with implicitly static functions.

return.name: Return
return.description: Returns a value or exits a void-result body. Async body results differ from their callable task carriers; preserve that distinction.

class.name: Class
class.description: Declares a class, public by default. Its members have indented bodies. Preserve inheritance, implemented interfaces, generic constraints, visibility and supported modifiers.

for.name: Counted Loop
for.syntax: for i from start to end step stepValue; for i = start; condition; i = next
for.description: One counted-loop keyword has two distinct semantics. The from/to/step header snapshots start, end and step once, in order, and includes the endpoint; omitted step is +1 and zero step throws. The =/semicolon form reevaluates its condition before each iteration and updates after the body or continue, not after break. Checked range overflow ends the snapshot range. Do not replace one form with the other.

each.name: Collection Iteration
each.syntax: each item in collection; each Type:item in collection; each key, value in collection
each.description: Iterates synchronously over a collection with an indented body. An explicit type precedes the item name. Two names deconstruct each element without tuple parentheses; collection evaluation remains once.
each.csharpEquivalent:
foreach (var item in items) { ... }
foreach (var (key, value) in dictionary) { ... }

while.name: While Loop
while.description: Evaluates the condition before each iteration and executes an indented body while true.

do.name: Do-While Loop
do.syntax: do indentedBody; while condition at the do indentation
do.description: Executes the body at least once. The trailing while condition is at the same indentation as do; there is no structural closer.

if.name: If Statement
if.syntax: if condition; else if condition; else
if.description: Conditional branches have indented bodies. else if and else align with if. Only the selected branch runs.

else.name: Alternative Branch
else.syntax: if condition; else if condition; else
else.description: Conditional branches have indented bodies. else if and else align with if. Only the selected branch runs.

await.name: Await
await.description:
Awaits an asynchronous operation.

Awaiting a .NET `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>` produces `T`. Awaiting a non-generic
carrier produces no value and cannot initialize a binding. `await` can also be
used as a statement. A custom type named `MyTask<T>` or a source declaration
named `Task<T>` is not automatically a .NET async carrier. Unsupported custom
awaitables are diagnosed or checked by generated C# validation, never inferred
from a name suffix.
await.csharpEquivalent:
var result = await FetchAsync();
await Task.Delay(1000);

!.name: Effects
!.description: Declares authoritative effects in the function header-clause region before the first body statement. Empty ! is a declared pure row. An omitted callback parameter, returned-callback or delegate contract is Unknown, as is explicit ! unknown in those positions. Unknown is not permission: strict invocation fails, even when the caller declares every known effect. Transporting Unknown can report Calor0425 when a row fit cannot be proved; permissive mode waives uncertainty, never known undeclared effects. ! unknown is not a callable's own effect declaration, binding row or lambda row. Effect variables bind with <! e> and occur in rows as ! e; a scoped variable named unknown retains its identity. Parameter rows follow type:name; output rows follow the output type; binding rows precede =; lambda rows precede =>. Preserve these distinct positions. Omitted binding and lambda rows can retain effects inferred from their initializer or body; they do not mean pure. In expression position, ! is logical negation, not an effect row. An unknown external call or manifest charge is not a metadata-resolution or purity proof.

=>.name: Postcondition or Lambda
=>.description: Declares a postcondition before the first body statement. result denotes the body return value, including async body results rather than task objects. In expression lambdas => is the lambda delimiter, not a postcondition.

break.name: Break
break.description: break exits the nearest loop; continue proceeds to its next iteration. A C#-form counted loop still performs its update after continue.

continue.name: Continue
continue.description: break exits the nearest loop; continue proceeds to its next iteration. A C#-form counted loop still performs its update after continue.

set.name: Assignment or Setter

examples.name: Assignment
examples.calor: set count count + 1

examples.name: Restricted Setter
examples.calor: set private

set.syntax: set target expression; set receiver[index] expression
set.description: Updates mutable bindings, fields or indexed storage. Indexed stores preserve left-to-right evaluate-once receiver, key and value evaluation, and dictionary updates are upserts rather than Add. Increment/decrement and compound assignment aliases are not separate expression forms. Inside a property or indexer, set declares a setter instead.

→.name: Return Type
→.description: Separates a callable signature's parameters from its output type. Async callable carriers and body results are distinct; contracts describe the body result.

property.name: Property
property.description: Declares a property with indented get, set or init accessors. Empty accessor bodies are auto-implemented; explicit bodies contain statements. Restricted accessor visibility follows its keyword, such as set private. Preserve defaults, modifiers and accessor effects.

field.name: Field
field.description: Declares a field with type before name, optional visibility and modifiers, and an optional initializer. Public is the default; preserve explicit private or protected visibility and readonly or static modifiers.

ctor.name: Constructor
ctor.description: Declares a constructor with an indented body. Explicit visibility precedes the parameter list. A base(args) or this(args) initializer is the first body clause; preserve ordered arguments and base versus same-type delegation.
ctor.csharpEquivalent:
public User(string name) { _name = name; }
public Admin(string name) : base(name) { }

interface.name: Interface
interface.description: Declares an interface with indented func signatures. Preserve generic variance, inherited interfaces, effective visibility and method contracts. Explicit visibility follows the name and type parameters.
interface.csharpEquivalent: public interface IRepository { void Save(Entity e); }

where.name: Generic Constraint
where.description: Adds generic constraints before a declaration body. Preserve each reference/value-type, constructor, base-type and interface requirement, rather than treating a type parameter as an unconstrained object. Inside a quantified contract, where introduces its guard instead of a generic constraint.

using.name: Import or Resource Lifetime

examples.name: Import
examples.calor: using System.Text

examples.name: Alias
examples.calor: using Text = System.Text

using.syntax: using System.Text; using Text = System.Text; using type:name = resource
using.description:
At compilation-unit scope, imports a namespace or declares an alias. In a function body, using introduces a resource and an indented body that disposes it on exit, including exceptions. Preserve the distinction between imports and resource lifetime management.

Typed resource headers preserve nullable annotations: `using System.IDisposable?:handle = input` keeps `handle` nullable inside the body.

Generated C# already imports `System`, so names such as `StringComparison` do not need an explicit `using System`. Source declarations, parameters, type parameters and aliases still participate in name lookup; the import does not override them.
using.csharpEquivalent:
using (var stream = File.OpenRead(path)) { ... }
using var connection = new SqlConnection(connStr);

try.name: Try
try.syntax: try; catch ExceptionType:name when condition; finally
try.description: Groups an indented try body with one or more catch clauses and/or finally cleanup. Catch types, binders and filters are optional; preserve exception selection, filter evaluation and cleanup on every exit.

throw.name: Throw or Rethrow
throw.description: Throws an exception expression. Bare throw rethrows the current exception inside a catch handler, preserving its original stack rather than constructing or throwing a replacement.

match.name: Match
match.syntax: match expression with indented case pattern → result arms
match.description: Matches an expression against ordered patterns. Expression arms use → followed by a result; statement arms have indented bodies. Preserve pattern guards and use return match when returning a match expression.
match.csharpEquivalent:
x switch { 1 => "one", 2 => "two", _ => "other" }
shape switch { Circle c => c.Area(), Rectangle r => r.Width * r.Height }

lock.name: Lock
lock.description: Executes an indented body while holding the selected monitor. Preserve evaluate-once lock-object selection and monitor release on returns and exceptions.

unsafe.name: Unsafe Block
unsafe.description: Introduces an indented unsafe body. Preserve unsafe effects and compile with unsafe support; the keyword is not permission to bypass diagnostics.

invariant.name: Invariant
invariant.description: Declares an invariant checked at the corresponding compilation-unit or type boundaries. Preserve the native contract AST and proof obligations, not an opaque runtime call.

op.name: Operator Overload
op.syntax: op + (type:left, type:right) → resultType; op implicit (type:value) → resultType
op.description: Declares an operator overload or conversion with an indented body. Conversion operators use implicit or explicit after op. An optional standalone ! effect row precedes contracts and body statements, as for functions. An explicit row is enforced and does not hide effects from callers. Direct source calls, including native enum-extension calls, preserve C# overload selection and argument mapping for implicit conversions at function, method and constructor inputs. Without a row, only intrinsic mutation and allocation are allowed; I/O, throwing and unknown calls remain rejected. The converter synthesizes explicit rows from the emitted native body. Operator effects are checked in every preprocessor configuration, up to eight condition symbols; larger conditional images fail effect checking rather than assuming purity. Preserve parameter order, result type and C# signature requirements.

pp.name: Conditional Compilation
pp.syntax: pp CONDITION; pp elif CONDITION; pp else
pp.description: Conditionally includes indented code. Chained pp clauses align with their opening pp. Conditions retain verbatim C# preprocessor text; preserve nested conditions and inactive branch contents under converter fidelity rules.

yield.name: Iterator Yield
yield.description: Yields a value from an iterator or ends iteration. Preserve lazy execution, suspension, iterator disposal and cleanup; do not materialize the sequence eagerly.

extends.name: Base Type
extends.description: Specifies a class's base type or inherited interfaces on an interface. Preserve generic arguments.

implements.name: Implemented Interface
implements.description: Specifies an interface implemented by a class or value type.

catch.name: Catch Block
catch.description: Catches exceptions with optional type, binder and filter. Its indented body follows try.

finally.name: Finally Block
finally.description: Runs the indented cleanup body on exit from try, including exceptions and returns.

get.name: Getter
get.description: Declares a property or indexer getter. An empty body is auto-implemented; an indented body contains statements.

init.name: Init Accessor
init.description: Declares an initialization-only property accessor. Preserve its visibility and body.

base.name: Base Constructor or Member
base.description: As the first constructor clause, calls the base constructor. In expressions, selects a base member.

this.name: Receiver, Constructor, Indexer or Extension Parameter
this.syntax: this.Member; this(args); this[int:index] → Type; this Type:receiver
this.description: Selects the current instance, delegates to another constructor as its first clause, declares an indexer, or marks the first extension-method parameter. These contexts are distinct.
this.csharpEquivalent: this.Member; : this(args); Type this[int index]; this Type receiver

case.name: Match Arm
case.syntax: case pattern → result; case pattern with indented statements
case.description: Declares an ordered expression or statement match arm. Use _ for a default pattern; preserve guards.

in.name: Iteration Source or Readonly Parameter
in.syntax: each item in source; in Type:value
in.description: Introduces a collection iteration source, or marks a readonly reference parameter in a signature.
in.csharpEquivalent: foreach (var item in source); in Type value

out.name: Output Parameter
out.description: Declares an output parameter in a signature. At a call site, pass the output argument with out.

from.name: Snapshot Range Start
from.syntax: for i from start to end step delta
from.description: Starts a counted loop whose start, end and step are evaluated once, in order.

to.name: Inclusive Snapshot Range End
to.syntax: for i from start to end step delta
to.description: Sets the inclusive endpoint of a snapshot counted loop. This is not a half-open slicing range.

step.name: Snapshot Range Step
step.syntax: for i from start to end step delta
step.description: Sets the snapshot range increment. Omission means +1; zero throws, and checked overflow ends iteration.

??.name: Null-Coalescing Expression
??.description: Evaluates the fallback only when the left operand is null.

?..name: Null-Conditional Access
?..description: Accesses the member only when the receiver is not null.

goto.name: Goto
goto.syntax: goto case expression; goto default; goto label
goto.description: Transfers control to a constant match case, the default arm, or a label written name:. Preserve the target and surrounding cleanup; goto case does not repeat the match selector's evaluation.

when.name: Pattern Guard or Catch Filter
when.syntax: case var name when condition → result; catch Type:name when condition
when.description: Adds a pattern guard or an exception filter. Evaluate it only after the corresponding pattern or exception selection.
when.csharpEquivalent: case var name when condition: statements; catch (Type name) when (condition)

enum.name: Enum
enum.description: Declares an enumeration with indented named members and optional explicit values. Preserve the underlying CLR type; omission defaults to int.
enum.csharpEquivalent:
public enum Status { Active, Inactive, Pending }
public enum Priority : byte { Low = 0, High = 1 }

delegate.name: Delegate
delegate.description: Declares a delegate signature at compilation-unit or class scope. Parameters are inline; an optional indented ! row retains the delegate's effect contract. Omission and ! unknown mean Unknown, while empty ! means Pure. Unknown is not a wildcard permission or a purity proof. Callback parameter and return contracts follow the same distinction. Preserve parameter modifiers and the result type.

event.name: Event
event.description: Declares an event, optionally with paired indented add and remove accessor bodies. Preserve the delegate type, visibility and supported modifiers. Named-module events are static; ordinary classes may explicitly declare a static event. Converter preservation of an unsupported event shape is not an authoring spelling. The complete example demonstrates declaration only. Native event subscription and unsubscription statements are not admitted yet; do not write retired section markers or invent +=/-= statements. Convert original C# when preservation is needed.

add.name: Event Add Accessor
add.syntax: event Handler:Changed with an indented add body
add.description: Declares the custom event subscription accessor. Pair it with remove and preserve all statements.

remove.name: Event Remove Accessor
remove.syntax: event Handler:Changed with an indented remove body
remove.description: Declares the custom event unsubscription accessor. Pair it with add and preserve all statements.

record.name: Record
record.description: Declares a C# record class. Positional parameters retain their constructor defaults and public init properties. Indent properties and methods beneath the header. C# supplies value equality, hashing, ToString, deconstruction and with/copy behavior. Derived positional records use `record D (int:X, int:Y) : B(X)`. Record structs, partial or nested declarations and unrepresented member variants remain exact converter-owned C# fallback, not native records.
record.csharpEquivalent: public record Point(int X, int Y);
